top.en: Actually, only the Chinese server translates Twitch's title as 'Source of Plague'. For example, the Korean server's title for Twitch is '역병 쥐' (Plague Rat), which is a direct translation of the English original. Furthermore, only the Chinese server uses champion titles instead of names as the default identifier. In other words, on Riot-operated servers, the loading screen, in-game chat, and tab menu all display the champion's actual name, not the title like in the Chinese server. Titles are basically only visible on the champion details page. The phenomenon in the Chinese server where titles are used more often than names (like 'Ashe' being called 'Frost Archer' more often than 'Ashe') is the exact opposite on Riot servers, and even more extreme, because at least Chinese players can see the champion name on the loading screen and tab menu when a skin is equipped, whereas on Riot servers, titles are truly only visible on the details page. After saying all that, my point is that it's highly unlikely Canna intended to use Twitch's title as some kind of taunt. Not only is the Korean title not 'Source of Plague', but many people playing on Riot servers don't even know what the titles are. When the news of Canna being [~0:flamed] reached international forums, I even saw people guessing it was because the streaming platform 'Twitch' is blocked in China, and they didn't even consider the title. I hope everyone thinks about the plausibility of rumors before spreading them.

thread.en:
On the first day of the 2020 MSC, during a match against TES, Canna (then T1 top laner) hovered Twitch during the first pick phase, then switched to Trundle and locked it in. Although these two champions are close in the KR server selection menu, they aren't right next to each other. Since it was during the pandemic and T1 already had a lot of haters, a rumor spread quickly that Canna was trying to use the 'Plague Rat' title to mock people.
However, in every other server, only the CN server translates Twitch's title as 'Plague Rat'. For example, the KR server title '역병 쥐' is a direct translation of the English 'the plague rat'. Furthermore, only the CN server uses champion titles as the default name instead of the champion's actual name. In official servers, the loading screen, chat, and tab menu show the champion's real name. Titles are basically only visible in the champion details page. The CN server phenomenon where titles are more common than names (like 'Ashe' being called 'Frost Archer') is the exact opposite in official servers. My point is, it's highly unlikely Canna was trying to use Twitch's title to mock anyone. Not only is the KR title not 'Plague Rat', but many players on official servers don't even know what the titles are. After the news of Canna being flamed reached international forums, I even saw people guessing it was because the streaming platform 'Twitch' is blocked in China, and they didn't even think about the title. I hope everyone thinks about the logic of a rumor before spreading it.
